theme_detail: How is additive redefining U.S. drone manufacturing?
Professional 3D Printing, Now Within Your Reach.
Why does industrial filament still come with so many trade-offs?
It's about building a production system the business can trust
For many metal AM applications, the answer is sintering

talk_track.claim: "We've reserved an HP MJF 1200. No payment needed, plus we get 20% off parts and up to $10,000 in credit."
talk_track.counter: Take the offer seriously, it is a good one. Then ask the question it avoids: the machine does not ship until early 2027. What are they producing between now and then? The 20% parts discount routes their volume to HP's own service bureau, so for the next two quarters they are outsourcing production and building a dependency, not building a capability. The credit is only redeemable against a machine that does not exist yet. Ask what happens to the credit if the ship date slips.

talk_track.claim: "HP is everywhere. Their marketing is far ahead of yours."
talk_track.counter: Be precise instead of defensive. HP runs 18 creatives on one platform, 36 live instances, and 97% of their biggest flight landed in the United States. What they do well is concentrate: one teaser took 500K-1M impressions in nineteen days around a launch. That is a burst strategy, not superior always-on marketing, and it is buyable. Meanwhile three of their live ads carry expired dates, one from October 2025. Volume is not rigor.

talk_track.claim: “HP's IF 600 HT is open materials, no lock-in.”
talk_track.counter: Open materials also means unvalidated materials. Ask who certifies the process for their application, and who they call when a build fails qualification.

talk_track.claim: “HP is the drone additive manufacturing leader.”
talk_track.counter: HP names three drone customers in its advertising: Blueflite, Unusual Machines, Firestorm Labs. That is a proof set, not a market. Ask for production volumes.

talk_track.claim: “HP is everywhere in additive right now.”
talk_track.counter: HP runs 18 creatives on one platform, LinkedIn, and zero on Meta. Its April teaser and February booth ad were still live in August. That is a narrow, under-maintained program, not omnipresence.

exposure: Production system and scale messaging. HP's “building a production system the business can trust” is Stratasys core ground and they are now advertising on it.
Industrial filament. The IF 600 HT overlaps Stratasys FDM directly and HP has moved from announcing it to handling objections about it.
Drone and UAV share of voice. HP holds 14 of 36 live instances on drones. Our Drone Dominance program is contesting the same feed.

Everything currently sold is a reservation against a machine that ships early 2027. The gap between the offer and the shipment is our best window and it closes when they ship.
Madrid agency running HP AM's EU LinkedIn media. Watch their payer feed for HP creative that has not yet appeared in the US.
O&P dropped from 5 instances to 2 in a week. If it does not come back, HP has deprioritised a vertical we also sell into.

spend_method: Dollars are derived at render time by tools/spend_model.py, never stored. Ads with no disclosed impressions are reported as not disclosed, never imputed.
